key: he sighs and says he has no change
name: ch17_chaiwala_no_change
alt: A customer holds out a large note at a tea stall, then the view from behind the counter shows the tea seller's nearly empty cash tin and a queue of waiting customers.
scene: A split-panel illustration with a thin vertical divider. LEFT panel: a roadside tea stall seen from the customer's side, a steel kettle steaming on a small stove and glass tumblers on a wooden counter. A young office worker in a light blue shirt with a laptop bag holds out a large purple note toward the tea seller, a thin man in his forties in a vest and checked lungi, who raises both palms with a sigh. A small red angry squiggle floats above the customer's head. RIGHT panel: the same moment seen from behind the counter, over the tea seller's shoulder. In front of him sits an open steel cash tin with only a few coins and two small notes inside, and a small clock on the stall pole reads 8:30. Beyond the counter a queue of four more office workers waits for tea, implying many more. A thought bubble from the tea seller shows the coins draining away with a downward arrow. In the foreground the same customer, now understanding, pulls a small green note from his wallet with a softer face. Fresh early morning light. Labels: "YOUR SIDE" at the top of the left panel, "HIS SIDE" at the top of the right panel, and "8:30" on the small clock.

key: Every Sunday your father spends two hours
name: ch17_father_scooter_sunday
alt: On a Sunday morning, a grown son and his father wash an old scooter together while the father tells a story about a long trip, shown in a memory bubble.
scene: A narrow residential lane in front of a small house with a green gate and a potted plant, on a sunny Sunday morning. In the CENTRE stands an old cream-and-teal two-wheeler scooter with a round headlight and a spare wheel at the back, shining wet. On the RIGHT the father, a man in his sixties with grey hair, spectacles and a white vest over a checked lungi, wipes the seat with a cloth, smiling and talking. On the LEFT the son, in his late twenties in a coral T-shirt and track pants, squats by the front mudguard with a yellow cloth, laughing at the story. A bucket with soap suds and a mug sits on the ground between them, small water puddles around it. Above the father a large memory bubble shows the same scooter years ago on a winding hill road toward a temple on a hilltop, with a young version of the father riding and a small bag tied at the back, and a dashed line leads from the bubble to the father's mouth. A small calendar page hangs on the gate reading "SUN". Bright warm morning light, a gentle, affectionate mood. Label: "SUNDAY" at the top centre of the picture.

key: A family meeting about a cousin
name: ch17_wedding_guest_list_meeting
alt: Relatives sit around a living-room table for a wedding meeting while the uncle points only to the guest list and calmly listens to the bride's mother.
scene: A family living room in the evening with a sofa, a low wooden table and a ceiling fan. On the table lies a single sheet of paper with lines of names on it, and beside it a folded venue brochure pushed aside with a small grey "later" clock icon on it to show the venue can wait. On the LEFT the uncle chairing the meeting, a calm man in his sixties in a white kurta with spectacles, sits forward with one hand resting on the guest list and the other open toward the bride's mother, listening, head slightly tilted. On the RIGHT the bride's mother, a woman in her fifties in a plum silk saree, speaks with feeling, one hand on her chest; her speech bubble shows a small crowd of relatives with the number "200". Behind them on the sofa two more relatives, a man in a teal shirt and a young woman in an amber kurta, sit relaxed with tea cups, no longer defensive. A small green heart-shaped badge near the uncle shows understanding being given before any numbers. Warm lamp light, a relieved, cooperative mood. Label: "GUEST LIST" written on the sheet of paper on the table, large and readable.

key: In a Pune housing society, teenagers
name: ch17_society_cricket_two_ways
alt: On one side an angry secretary scolds teenage cricketers in a parking lot full of cars; on the other a friendly resident points them toward an open ground and hands them a tennis ball.
scene: A split-panel illustration with a thin vertical divider. LEFT panel: the parking area of a housing society, two parked cars, one with a cracked windscreen marked by a small jagged line. An angry society secretary, a heavy man in his fifties in a shirt and trousers, points a finger and waves a notice, his face red; three teenage boys in coral, teal and amber T-shirts stand with crossed arms and glares, one holding a hard leather ball and a bat, and a small circular arrow badge shows they will be back the next day. RIGHT panel: the same parking area in the evening; a friendly resident, a man in his forties in a plum kurta, crouches slightly with a smile and holds out a fluffy green tennis ball, while his other hand points to an open ground behind a building block labelled with a small sign "C". The same three boys look curious and relaxed; one is already taking the tennis ball, and a dashed amber arrow leads from the group to the open ground with a small cricket stump icon. Soft evening light. Labels: "FINE" at the top of the left panel, "THEIR SIDE" at the top of the right panel.

key: You board the wrong coach of an overnight
name: ch17_tte_wrong_coach
alt: Inside a night train coach, a passenger stands and apologises to a tired ticket examiner, who sighs and points toward a free berth further down the train.
scene: Inside an overnight sleeper train coach, seen down the aisle, with blue berths stacked on both sides, a small night light glowing and dark windows showing a few distant lights. In the CENTRE a young male passenger in his late twenties in a grey T-shirt stands in the aisle with his backpack, one hand on his chest, the other holding out his phone with a ticket on it, head bowed slightly in a sincere apology. Facing him on the RIGHT is the ticket examiner, a tired man in his fifties in a black coat over a white shirt, holding a clipboard with a chart, a pen behind his ear; his shoulders sag with a long sigh, and a small thought bubble above him shows another passenger shouting with a jagged red speech mark. On the LEFT two other passengers lie on their berths, one pretending to sleep with a blanket pulled up, another peeking out. A dashed amber arrow from the examiner's pointing hand leads off to the far end of the coach, toward a small inset showing an empty berth with a green tick and a small coin icon for the fare difference. Dim night lighting inside, but warm and calm. Label: "MY MISTAKE" above the young passenger.

key: Before asking your father to let you take
name: ch17_job_city_father_worries
alt: A young woman sits alone at a desk listing her father's likely worries, each matched with an answer, before talking with him at the dinner table.
scene: A split-panel illustration with a thin vertical divider. LEFT panel, late evening in a small bedroom: a young woman in her mid-twenties in a teal kurta sits at a desk with a table lamp, writing in a notebook. Above her three thought bubbles show her father's likely worries as simple icons: a grandmother with a walking stick, a phone with a broken heart (a cousin who stopped calling), and a medal or trophy (pride in her work at home). Next to each worry a small answer card with a green tick: a calendar with weekends marked, a video call screen marked "SUN", and a smiling cousin waving from a house. RIGHT panel, the dinner table the next day with a steel plate, rotis and a water jug: the same young woman sits across from her father, a man in his late fifties with grey hair, spectacles and a white kurta, who listens thoughtfully with his chin on his hand; the same three answer cards lie open on the table between them, and a dashed arrow links her notebook in the left panel to the cards on the table. The mood is calm, serious and respectful rather than tense. Labels: "HIS WORRIES" at the top of the left panel, "THE TALK" at the top of the right panel.
